current_registry_statement: An LVDT senses linear motion through AC-excited transformer windings and the position-dependent magnetic coupling of a movable ferromagnetic core, producing a differential secondary voltage. A strain-gauge displacement instrument instead infers motion from strain in a mechanical member or elastic element via a small resistance change in bonded gauges, commonly converted to voltage with a Wheatstone bridge. The latter requires a mechanical strain-to-displacement relationship and is not the same transduction mechanism as the LVDT.
proposed_statement: An LVDT senses mechanically coupled motion through changes in transformer coupling and differential output. A strain gage senses deformation through resistance change, commonly measured with a Wheatstone bridge; displacement then depends on the mechanical structure that converts motion to strain.
applicable_conditions: Strain-gage displacement depends on the instrumented mechanical element.
